fact: The World Bank's additional-financing paper records 'No' at December 2025 for the establishment of an electronic health record system, a new indicator with targets of Yes by December 2027 or 2028, and describes the EHR as something to be introduced.

The World Bank's results framework gives a baseline of 0 health facilities contracted with the national health insurance scheme holding an electronic health record system at December 2025, against a target of 50 (the results table also shows 60 and 70) by December 2028, out of about 335 contracted facilities; it does not separate primary clinics.

The World Bank paper says that since October 2025 the health ministry (MoH-UHC) has been responsible for the health and insurance systems layer, including the EHR, and that the EHR pilot is supported by the ministry's national health information system division, DSNISI.

The World Bank's additional financing of December 2025 pays for the EHR through performance-based conditions: EUR 866,112.50 on establishment of the system and EUR 173,223 for every 10 contracted facilities with an EHR, with USD 160,000 for equipment and implementation in the centres; no domestic budget line is stated.

The World Bank project paper of December 2025 sets costed, dated targets for the EHR under sub-component 3.1.2 (US$6.50 million for digitalising the insurance scheme): a pilot over a representative sample of primary, secondary and tertiary facilities and laboratories, the system established by 2027-2028 and 50 contracted facilities equipped by December 2028; this is a donor project plan, not a national strategy.

On 24 December 2025 the World Bank put forward additional financing (a EUR 60.6 million credit and US$11 million in grants) that adds new performance-based conditions for establishing an electronic health record system in facilities contracted under the national health insurance scheme, starting with a pilot.

The health ministry's SNIS procedures manual states that DHIS2 was adopted as the national integrated platform for SNIS data and scaled up to all health facilities in the country from 2018; the facilities it names as entering reports are USP, private facilities (EPS), CHP, CHR and CHU.

The manual (April 2022) requires each health facility (USP, EPS, CHP, CHR, CHU) to key its own validated monthly and quarterly activity reports (RMA/RTA), compiled from paper registers, into DHIS2 before the 5th of the following month and also to send a paper copy to the prefectoral health directorate (DPS), which validates the entries in DHIS2 by the 20th.

The manual (April 2022) places coordination of the SNIS under the health ministry's Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire et de l'Informatique (DSNISI), whose national SNIS pool is charged with maintaining and updating DHIS2.

The manual states that the ministry has a strategic plan for strengthening the SNIS (PSSNIS/PSRSNIS) for 2018-2022, aligned to the PNDS 2017-2022 and following a first plan for 2013-2017, and that DHIS2 was adopted as the national platform in the context of that plan.
The manual (April 2022) names no budget line for the SNIS or DHIS2; it lists seeking partners to finance the SNIS among the duties of both the regional and the national SNIS pools.

The Togo Digital 2025 strategy (April 2021) plans, under access to basic social services, the digitalisation of care pathways alongside the roll-out of universal health coverage, including a digital and centralised medical record, online appointment booking and a digital vaccination booklet, and lists 'constitution of a single medical record' among the public services to digitise; it describes these as to be developed, not as existing.

DHIS2 (HISP) states that when Togo moved its routine immunisation (EPI) reporting off DVD-MT into the national HMIS on DHIS2, data entry and analysis were decentralised down to the facility level; it gives EPI report completeness of 99.1% in 2018 and 99.3% in 2019 and on-time submission rising from 38.2% to 83% (both printed as 2019).

DHIS2 (HISP) states that Togo implemented the DHIS2 immunization package and data quality tool with the support of Gavi; the statement covers the immunisation reporting within the national DHIS2, not the whole system, and no domestic funding is mentioned.

WHO Togo's 2024 annual report states that Togo uses DHIS2 to collect health data in all districts and that, despite good command of the tools and a working quality-control system, completeness rates remain unstable: 91% in 2017, a peak of 96.5% in 2018, then a fall to 89.2% in 2021; it gives no numerator or denominator and does not say which facilities report or where the data is keyed.

WHO Togo reports that in 2024, through the Benin-Burkina Faso-Niger-Togo (BBNT) initiative supported by WHO and the Global Fund, Togo strengthened its capacity to analyse and use the data extracted from DHIS2 on malaria, tuberculosis and HIV, hepatitis and STIs, the analysis leading to a roadmap of corrective measures; it gives no counts of staff or facilities.

The Global Fund's Office of the Inspector General states that timeliness and completeness of reported data improved throughout Grant Cycle 6 (2021 to 2023) and that for 2023 DHIS2 reporting completeness reached 100% for HIV, 94% for malaria and 93% for TB, with timeliness of 94%, 82% and 87%; it gives no numerators or denominators and does not say where the reports are keyed.

The OIG states that the health ministry's Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire et de l'Informatique (DSNIS) manages and develops the existing health information systems, naming DHIS2; the position is undated, so the report's published date is used.

The OIG states that Global Fund investment in Togo's health management information system and related systems rose from EUR 2.3 million in Grant Cycle 5 to EUR 7.3 million in Grant Cycle 6 and EUR 9.8 million in Grant Cycle 7 (2024 to 2026), budgets that also cover surveys, strategic plan reviews and programme supervision; it names no domestic budget line.

The OIG states that Togo has no coordinated national digitalisation strategy for health covering DHIS2, the planned eLMIS and the medical store's ERP, and no data quality improvement plan for the health system, a national data quality review being planned for 2025; the statement is about a strategy across the systems, not a plan for DHIS2 alone, and is undated, so the report's published date is used.

The health ministry's monitoring and evaluation plan for the PNDS 2023-2027, validated on 6 October 2023, requires each health facility to key its validated monthly or quarterly activity report (RMA/RTA) into DHIS2 before the 5th of the following month, the facility's SNIS respondent doing the entry, and to send the paper copy to the prefectoral health directorate (DPS) by the same date; it also sets the 20th as the deadline at DPS level for the reports to be entered in DHIS2.

The plan (validated 6 October 2023) names the facilities producing and keying SNIS reports as the peripheral care units (USP), where the facility head is the SNIS respondent, and the CHP, CHR and CHU hospitals, where a data or statistics officer is; it says the CHR and CHU data are taken into account by the health district in whose area they sit.

The health ministry's plan gives the SNIS report completeness rate as 96.5% in 2021, defined as the number of health facilities that keyed a complete SNIS report into DHIS2 over the total number of health facilities due to key SNIS reports, sourced to the health statistics yearbook; it prints the rate only, without the counts, covers all facilities and not primary clinics alone, notes duplicate entries in hospital data as a known bias, and gives timeliness of 77.3% in 2021.

The plan (validated 6 October 2023) states that DHIS2 is the SNIS platform chosen by the health ministry, that coordination of the SNIS is the responsibility of the ministry's Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire et de l'Informatique (DSNISI), and that the national SNIS pool maintains and updates DHIS2.

The monitoring and evaluation plan of the PNDS 2023-2027, validated on 6 October 2023, names DHIS2 as the SNIS platform, sets yearly targets to 2027 for SNIS completeness (97.2% in 2023 to 100% in 2027), timeliness (78.8% to 85%) and data quality audits, and schedules and costs an annual SNIS review for each year from 2023 to 2027.

The plan (validated 6 October 2023) names no budget line for the SNIS or DHIS2; it lists seeking partners to finance the SNIS among the duties of the national and regional SNIS pools and names mobilising the resources needed for optimal use of DHIS2 as a requirement of the central directorates.
